items.title: The 2029 tipping point: Western populations are about to start shrinking, piling pressure on public finances
items.body: Moody's predicts that the world's aging populations will have fundamental impacts on the global economy and lead to difficult policy decisions.

items.title: Men are losing ground in the labor market. Here's why
items.body: Women outnumbered men in the workforce for eight straight months as of September, according to one analysis.

items.title: Labor market faltered in September as jobs increased by just 29,000, unemployment rate rose to 4.2%
items.body: Nonfarm payrolls rose by just 29,000 in September, well below the 84,000 forecast, and the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said.

items.title: The September jobs report will be released Friday. Here's what to expect
items.body: Wall Street is looking for job growth of 84,000 to close out the summer.

items.title: Fed’s preferred gauge showed core inflation at 3.0% in August, much lighter than expected
items.body: The personal consumption expenditures price index was projected to show an annual gain of 3.7% on headline and 3.3% for core, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

items.title: Private sector jobs rose by 90,000 in September, better than expected, ADP reports
items.body: Private job creation picked up in September after a brief slowdown.

items.title: The Fed's main inflation measure will be released Wednesday. Here's what to expect
items.body: Data is expected to show ongoing price pressures and consumers who nevertheless continue to spend.

items.title: Consumer optimism slides to lowest since 2014 as fears escalate over rising prices and jobs
items.body: The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index tumbled to 81.9, a decline of 6.7 points and a reading well below the forecast for 89.
